description:
Officially granted university status in 1964, the University of Strathclyde has 22,000 students from 100 different countries. The university's only campus is located in the heart of Glasgow, Scotland. It was named “University of the Year” in 2012 and “Entrepreneurial University of the Year” in 2013 by the Strathclyde Times.

The University is known for its Faculty of Business, which is in close contact with the industry. The University of Strathclyde is among 55 universities globally that have received “triple accreditation” by three significant associations. The university has recently opened a new campus in Delhi. Many of its programs, such as product design and innovation, modern languages, and international business, are designed with industry experts. The University has Scotland's most significant engineering faculty and Europe's largest electrical power-based engineering and energy research facility.

Life is pretty fun at the university, ranked 36th in the Times University Guide 2020, 51st in the Guardian University Guide 2020, and 300th in the QS World University Rankings.

The Strathclyde Center for Technology and Innovation develops the university's research output. In the 2014 Research Excellence Framework, the university was ranked among the UK's top 20 research-intensive universities. The University has the best Physics department in the UK. The Electrical and Electronics Engineering department is the first in Scotland.

About 1,500 students stay on campus, while about 400 live in university dormitories within walking distance of the campus. Strathclyde residence halls are arranged in apartments where students share common areas such as the kitchen. All first-year undergraduate students are guaranteed accommodation. A web-based service offered by the university facilitates accessible communication between hosts and students seeking private accommodation.
